metas.name: Poetry
metas.description:
A mind begins to dissolve even as it learns to see. A grandmother in early Alzheimer's takes a poetry class and discovers her grandson's part in a terrible crime; the homework — really look at an apple, a tree — becomes the plot.

A sixty-something woman, faced with the discovery of a heinous family crime and in the early stages of Alzheimer's disease, finds strength and purpose when she enrolls in a poetry class.

metas.name: The Earth Is Blue as an Orange
metas.description:
Inside a real war, a family directs its own war movie. In the Donbas front-line town of Krasnohorivka, a mother and her kids shoot a fiction film about their lives between shelling — the camera as the household's way of staying sane, years before 2022 made the footage prophetic.

To cope with the daily trauma of living in a war-zone, Anna and her children are making a film together about their life in the most surreal surroundings.

metas.name: Céline and Julie Go Boating
metas.description:
Two women hack a melodrama from the audience seats. A librarian and a magician find a haunted house where the same Victorian drama replays daily; they enter it, swap places with its characters and start stealing the plot with the help of magic sweets.

A mysteriously linked pair of young women find their daily lives preempted by a strange boudoir melodrama that plays itself out in a hallucinatory parallel reality.

metas.name: Bashu, the Little Stranger
metas.description:
A war orphan is adopted across a language barrier. A boy from bombed Khuzestan washes up in a northern rice village where nobody speaks Arabic and the war is a rumour; a widowed farmer takes him in against the whole village's suspicion.

An Iranian boy is lost after fleeing home for his life; his family has been killed during the Iran-Iraq war. He's saved and trained by a middle-aged woman.

metas.name: Kaili Blues
metas.description:
Past, present and dream share one road through this town. A country doctor rides to find his nephew; halfway in, the film becomes a single 41-minute take through a village where time has stopped behaving — and nobody comments on it.

While travelling the countryside to locate his nephew, a small town doctor finds himself interacting with people from his past and future.

metas.name: In the Basement
metas.description:
The film goes looking for what Austrians keep under the house. A documentary of suburban basements — Nazi memorabilia shrines, shooting ranges, doll collections, dungeons — each owner proudly giving the tour, each room arranged like a still life.

A documentary that reveals what its subjects do in their respective basements.

metas.name: About Elly
metas.description:
A kindly told lie keeps compounding. Friends invite a shy teacher on a seaside trip to set her up with a divorced friend; she vanishes on the second day, and every small politeness from the first day returns as evidence. Asghar Farhadi's storytelling engine, running rawer here.

The mysterious disappearance of a kindergarten teacher during a picnic in the north of Iran is followed by a series of misadventures for her fellow travelers.

metas.name: Long Day's Journey into Night
metas.description:
A noir dissolves into the dream it was always having. A man returns to Kaili hunting a woman from twenty years ago; the final hour is one unbroken take inside a dream, in 3D in cinemas — the rare film where you can feel it cross over.

A man went back to Guizhou, found the tracks of a mysterious woman. He recalls the summer he spent with her twenty years ago.

metas.name: Le Bonheur
metas.description:
Happiness becomes the most frightening special effect. A carpenter with a wife, lover and two children, photographed in sunlit Renoir colours, narrating his contentment — and the prettier it gets, the more quietly monstrous the arithmetic becomes.

François, a young carpenter, lives a happy, uncomplicated life with his wife Thérèse and their two small children. One day he meets Emilie, a clerk in the local post office.

metas.name: Save the Green Planet!
metas.description:
A conspiracy theorist who might be right gets played at full scream. A beekeeper kidnaps a chemicals CEO he believes is an alien prince; comedy, torture chamber, police procedural and apocalypse keep swapping places until the film lands somewhere genuinely sad.

Byeong-gu believes that the world is on the verge of an alien invasion, and sets out to save the world.

metas.name: Lightning Over Water
metas.description:
Two directors film a death; one of them is the dying man. Ray, terminal with cancer, co-directs his own ending — rehearsals, hospital corridors, arguments about whether the camera should be there at all. The complicit-camera question, asked by the subject himself.

Director 'Nicholas Ray' is eager to complete a final film before his imminent death from cancer. Wim Wenders is working on his own film Hammett (1983) in Hollywood, but flies to New York to help Ray realize his final wish. Ray's original intent is to make a fiction film about a dying painter who sails to China to find a cure for his disease. He and Wenders discuss this idea, but it is obviously unrealistic given Ray's state of health.

metas.name: Paradise: Love
metas.description:
Both sides are performing in this transaction. A Viennese mother on a Kenyan beach holiday buys companionship from young men who run it as a business with scripts of their own; Seidl never tells you which performance is sadder.

Teresa, a fifty-year-old Austrian mother, travels to the paradise of the beaches of Kenya, seeking out love from African boys. But she must confront the hard truth that on the beaches of Kenya, love is a business.

metas.name: Crimson Gold
metas.description:
Class humiliation unfolds at the pace of a pizza delivery. A Tehran courier, slighted in a jewellery store he could never shop in, returns with a gun; written by Kiarostami from a real case, and the city itself does most of the accusing.

An Iranian pizza delivery man sees the worst of corruption and social unbalance in his city and is driven to crime.

metas.name: Suzhou River
metas.description:
A city remembers a woman who may never have existed. A videographer-for-hire drifts along Shanghai's river between a mermaid-performing girlfriend and the lost love of a smuggler who swears they're the same person. Vertigo rebuilt from motorbike rides and river grime.

After getting out of prison, small-time crook Mardar stumbles upon a woman who looks exactly like his long-lost lover.

metas.name: Muriel, or The Time of Return
metas.description:
A country edits out its war in real time. In Boulogne, a widow and her stepson — back from Algeria, unable to say what happened to a girl named Muriel — circle each other in conversations cut a half-second too early, like memory flinching.

In the seaside town of Boulogne, no one seems to be able to cope with their past, least of all Hélène, an antique furniture saleswoman, her stepson Bernard, and her former lover Alphonse.

metas.name: Turtles Can Fly
metas.description:
Children run a war economy before the war officially starts. In a Kurdish refugee camp on the Iraq–Turkey border, kids clear minefields for resale and a boy called Satellite installs dishes so the village can watch the invasion coming on TV.

Near the Iraqi-Turkish border on the eve of an American invasion, refugee children, like 13-year-old Kak (Ebrahim), gauge and await their fate.

metas.name: Alice in the Cities
metas.description:
Two stranded people temporarily adopt each other. A blocked German writer and a nine-year-old girl abandoned at an airport cross America and then the Ruhr looking for a grandmother who may not exist at the address anyone remembers.

A German journalist is saddled with a nine-year-old girl after encountering her mother at a New York airport.

metas.name: There Is No Evil
metas.description:
Capital punishment becomes an ordinary job worked in four shifts. Four stories about men ordered to pull the lever in Iran — a family man, a conscript, a soldier on leave, a doctor with a past — each segment quietly redefining what refusal costs. Filmed in secret; won Berlin's Golden Bear.

The four stories that are variations on the crucial themes of moral strength and the death penalty that ask to what extent individual freedom can be expressed under a despotic regime and its seemingly inescapable threats.

metas.name: Oxhide
metas.description:
A family lives inside 50 square metres and one failing business. The director films her own parents in their Beijing apartment and leather shop, in nine static shots, playing a version of herself; the bag shop is dying and everyone discusses dinner instead.

Director Liu Jiayin casts her parents and herself as fictionalized members of a Beijing family that has fallen on hard times and ekes out an existence by making bags out of oxhide for sale.

metas.name: Out 1
metas.description:
Paris becomes a conspiracy that may just be theatre people. Nearly thirteen hours: two experimental theatre troupes rehearsing Aeschylus, a drifter intercepting mysterious letters, and a secret society that might be a game everyone agreed to forget. That length is by design — it changes your sense of what a film's runtime is for.

Following the May 1968 civil unrest in France, a deaf-mute and a con artist simultaneously stumble upon the remnants of a secret society.

metas.name: Right Now, Wrong Then
metas.description:
The same day is told twice, with the pronouns changed. A director visits a town, meets a painter, drinks, flatters, fumbles; then the film restarts and plays it again with small shifts of honesty — a controlled experiment in how little has to change for everything to.

A married film director falls for a young painter - twice.

metas.name: No Bears
metas.description:
From exile inside his own country, a director directs by laptop. Panahi, banned from filming and travel, rents a room near the Turkish border and shoots remotely — until the village's own drama reaches through the screen. He was arrested before it premiered; the film knows something like that is coming.

Two parallel love stories in which the partners are thwarted by hidden, inevitable obstacles, the force of superstition, and the mechanics of power.

metas.name: The Wind Will Carry Us
metas.description:
A film crew waits for a death they're too polite to name. Tehran engineers idle in a Kurdish village, officially digging, actually waiting to film an old woman's funeral ritual; almost nothing happens, at the pace of wind over wheat, and it's somehow utterly complete.

Irreverent city engineer Behzad comes to a rural village in Iran to keep vigil for a dying relative. In the meanwhile the film follows his efforts to fit in with the local community and how he changes his own attitudes as a result.

metas.name: Sherlock Jr.
metas.description:
A projectionist climbs into the screen to fix the plot from inside. A century old and still the cleanest film ever made about wanting to live in the observed layer instead of the real one; the montage where the scenery changes around him mid-step has never been topped.

A film projectionist longs to be a detective, and puts his meagre skills to work when he is framed by a rival for stealing his girlfriend's father's pocketwatch.

metas.name: Sullivan's Travels
metas.description:
A comedy director goes slumming to learn suffering, and learns the value of comedy instead. He disguises himself as a tramp to research a serious film, gets the research, and the conclusion lands in a prison screening room full of laughing men.

A Hollywood director sets out to experience life as a homeless person in order to gain relevant life experience for his next movie.

metas.name: Zelig
metas.description:
A man's personality becomes whoever is standing nearest. A mockumentary about a 1920s "human chameleon" who becomes a boxer beside boxers and a rabbi beside rabbis, assembled from fake newsreels and real historians playing along — conformity as a superpower and a diagnosis.

"Documentary" about a man who can look and act like whoever he's around, and meets various famous people.

metas.name: The Purple Rose of Cairo
metas.description:
A film character notices he's being watched, and steps out. A Depression-era waitress goes to the same romance every day until its hero leaves the screen for her — and the other characters, stuck mid-plot, have to improvise without him.

During the Depression in 1935 New Jersey, a lonely waitress with an abusive husband who takes comfort from the movies is stunned when a movie character walks off the screen and into the real world, offering her the hope of a happi...

metas.name: Groundhog Day
metas.description:
A loop, it turns out, can be a curriculum. A weatherman relives one day until the day is no longer the constraint — the rare infinitely-referenced film that is also exactly as good as its reputation.

A curmudgeonly weatherman finds himself stuck in a time loop and is forced to relive the same day over and over again.

metas.name: Timecrimes
metas.description:
In this time loop, a man becomes his own haunting. A guy with binoculars, a bandaged stranger, a scientist with a tank — three trips through one hour, each pass reassigning who the villain is. The tightest loop mechanics ever filmed, on a Spanish hillside with almost no budget.

A man accidentally gets into a time machine and travels back in time nearly an hour. Finding himself will be the first of a series of disasters of unforeseeable consequences.

metas.name: Beyond the Infinite Two Minutes
metas.description:
A café monitor shows the room two minutes in the future. Shot on a phone in apparent single takes by a Kyoto theatre troupe; the staff keep feeding instructions to their past selves and the recursion stacks up like a card trick that keeps working.

A cafe owner discovers that the TV in his cafe suddenly shows images from the future, but only two minutes into the future.

metas.name: The Man from Earth
metas.description:
An entire science-fiction epic is conducted as a conversation. A professor tells his colleagues he's a 14,000-year-old caveman who stopped ageing; nobody leaves the room, no effect is ever shown, and the argument itself becomes the spectacle.

A professor's impromptu retirement party becomes a mysterious interrogation when he reveals to his colleagues that he has a longer and stranger past than they can imagine.

metas.name: Being John Malkovich
metas.description:
A portal into someone else's head, rented out at $200 a session. A puppeteer finds a door on floor 7½ that drops you behind Malkovich's eyes for fifteen minutes — the eerie business of living inside another person's view played as office farce, then as tragedy.

A puppeteer discovers a portal that leads literally into the head of movie star John Malkovich.

metas.name: The Double
metas.description:
A man is replaced by the version of himself with better settings. A clerk nobody notices meets his double, who is identical and effortlessly everything he isn't; Dostoevsky rebuilt as a clanking bureaucratic nightmare with Jesse Eisenberg against himself.

The unenviable life of a government-agency clerk takes a horrific turn with the arrival of a new co-worker who is both his exact physical double and his opposite otherwise--he's a confident, charismatic ladies' man.

metas.name: Mr. Nobody
metas.description:
A life is told as the full tree of its branches. The last mortal human, aged 117, tells his biography and keeps contradicting himself, because every childhood coin-flip version happened; the film refuses to prune, and the unpruned version is the portrait.

A boy stands on a station platform as a train is about to leave. Should he go with his mother or stay with his father? Infinite possibilities arise from this decision. As long as he doesn't choose, anything is possible.

metas.name: The Science of Sleep
metas.description:
Dreams here are a handmade TV studio inside a shy man's skull. A Mexican illustrator in Paris can't keep his dream-logic — cardboard cameras, cellophane water, a one-second time machine — from leaking into the courtship he's botching while awake.

A man entranced by his dreams and imagination is love-struck with a French woman and feels he can show her his world.

metas.name: Dave Made a Maze
metas.description:
A living-room fort turns out to be bigger, and lethal, inside. An artist builds a cardboard maze he claims he can't finish or escape; his girlfriend leads a rescue party in with documentary crew in tow. Every trap is cardboard. It kills people anyway.

Dave, an artist who has yet to complete anything significant in his career, builds a fort in his living room out of pure frustration, only to wind up trapped by the fantastical pitfalls, booby traps, and critters of his own creation.

metas.name: One Cut of the Dead
metas.description:
A film set survives its own film. The first half-hour is a wobbly one-take zombie short; then the film rewinds and shows you the production, and every wobble becomes a joke with a fuse on it. Engineered joy — don't read anything else about it.

Things go badly for a hack director and film crew shooting a low budget zombie movie in an abandoned WWII Japanese facility, when they are attacked by real zombies.

metas.name: Swiss Army Man
metas.description:
A friendship forms with a corpse who is also a toolkit. A castaway rides a flatulent body to shore and teaches it how to be a person — jet-ski farts, earnest puppet dioramas of ordinary life, and a sincerity that sneaks up on the gross-out premise.

A hopeless man stranded on a deserted island befriends a dead body, and together they go on a surreal journey to get home.

metas.name: Everything Everywhere All at Once
metas.description:
A multiverse becomes the setting for a family argument. A laundromat owner audits her failed lives across universes — chef, starlet, rock, sausage-fingered pianist — and the loudest sci-fi machinery of the decade is aimed at a tax audit and a daughter.

A middle-aged Chinese immigrant is swept up into an insane adventure in which she alone can save existence by exploring other universes and connecting with the lives she could have led.

metas.name: The Lobster
metas.description:
A dating regime runs on a deadline and a species change. Single people get 45 days in a hotel to find a partner or be transformed into an animal of their choice; everyone speaks like a form being filled in, and the flatness is the romance and the horror at once.

In a dystopian near future, according to the laws of The City, single people are taken to The Hotel, where they are obliged to find a romantic partner in 45 days or they're transformed into beasts and sent off into The Woods.

metas.name: Lars and the Real Girl
metas.description:
A whole town agrees, as treatment, to believe. A painfully shy man orders a life-size doll and introduces her as his girlfriend; on a doctor's advice the whole town plays along — church seat, volunteer shifts, the works. The premise sounds like a sketch; the execution is a study in communal gentleness.

A delusional young man strikes up an unconventional relationship with a doll he finds on the Internet.

metas.name: Brigsby Bear
metas.description:
Fandom becomes a survival structure. A man raised in a bunker on a fake children's show — hundreds of episodes made only for him — is rescued into a world where the show never existed, and decides the only sane response is to film its finale himself.

After being freed from his life in an underground bunker, a man sets out to make a movie of the only TV show he has ever known.

metas.name: What We Do in the Shadows
metas.description:
Four vampires fail at flatshare administration. Wellington's undead argue about the dishes roster, dress codes for clubs and a rival werewolf pack ("we're werewolves, not swearwolves") in deadpan documentary form. Deliberately, disarmingly light.

Viago, Deacon, and Vladislav are vampires who are struggling with the mundane aspects of modern life, like paying rent, keeping up with the chore wheel, trying to get into nightclubs, and overcoming flatmate conflicts.

metas.name: Song of the Sea
metas.description:
A selkie myth is drawn the way the sea draws on rock. A mute little girl is the last seal-child; her brother resents her for their mother's death, and the rescue journey is rendered in spirals, knots and watercolour geometry.

Ben, a young Irish boy and his little sister, Saoirse, a girl who can turn into a seal, go on an adventure to free the fairies and save the spirit world.

metas.name: Ernest & Celestine
metas.director: Stéphane Aubier, Vincent Patar, Benjamin Renner
metas.description:
A bear and a mouse are outlawed by both their societies for their friendship. Bears live above, mice below, each raised on horror stories about the other; a watercolor heist and a double trial later, the film has made its whole case with a pencil line and a piano.

The story of an unlikely friendship between a bear, Ernest, and a young mouse named Celestine.

metas.name: Robot Dreams
metas.description:
A friendship is conducted entirely without dialogue, in 1980s New York, between a dog and a mail-order robot. They dance to Earth, Wind & Fire on roller skates; a beach closing separates them; the film then does the bravest thing a family film can do with its ending. Wordless, and it earns tears honestly.

The adventures and misfortunes of Dog and Robot in New York City during the 1980s.

metas.name: Flow
metas.description:
Animals cooperate after the humans vanish, with no speech and no villain. A cat that fears water survives a flood aboard a drifting boat shared with a capybara, a lemur, a secretary bird and a dog; made in Blender by a tiny Latvian team, and the water alone justifies it.

Cat is a solitary animal, but as its home is devastated by a great flood, he finds refuge on a boat populated by various species, and will have to team up with them despite their differences.

metas.name: Marcel the Shell with Shoes On
metas.description:
An inch-high shell with a breadcrumb for a hat processes fame and loss at full sincerity. A documentarian films his tiny Airbnb cohabitant, whose missing community and ill grandmother turn stop-motion cuteness into something quietly devastating about scale and care.

A cash-strapped documentary maker decides to make his newest documentary about a mollusk shell he finds living in his Airbnb with his friends.

metas.name: Gates of Heaven
metas.description:
Two pet cemeteries — one failed, one thriving — and the people who can explain everything except themselves. Morris points the camera, asks almost nothing, and owners, renderers and salesmen deliver monologues that keep slipping from pets into the meaning of a life. His first film; it made Herzog eat a shoe.

A documentary about a pet cemetery in California, and the people who have pets buried there.

metas.name: Fast, Cheap & Out of Control
metas.description:
Four obsessions rhyme: a lion tamer, a topiary gardener, a mole-rat scientist and a robot engineer, intercut until their separate monologues start answering each other. The meaning emerges from the cuts themselves.

An exploration of the careers of four unrelated professionals: a lion tamer, a robotics expert, a topiary gardener, and a naked mole rat specialist.

metas.name: Between the Folds
metas.description:
Origami is followed where it stops being a craft: physicists folding proteins and deployable space lenses, a man who folds a single sheet into a full orchestra, theorems proved with creases. Ten paper artists and scientists, one shared conviction that a fold is a way of thinking.

Depicts a cast of fine artists and eccentric scientists (from MIT and NASA) who have devoted their lives to the unlikely medium of modern origami. Through their determination to reinterpret the world in paper, they arouse a fascin...

metas.name: A Glitch in the Matrix
metas.description:
Simulation theory is treated as a belief system with adherents, not a thought experiment. Speakers testify through digital avatars — itself the film's best argument — while clips and Philip K. Dick's 1977 "I am speaking to you from a replica" speech do the rest.

Documentary filmmaker Rodney Ascher tackles the question "are we living in a simulation?" with testimony, philosophical evidence and scientific explanation in his quest for the answer.

metas.name: The Mole Agent
metas.description:
An 83-year-old widower is hired to infiltrate a nursing home as a spy, and keeps forgetting to spy because the residents need a friend. A detective kit, a private investigator, hidden-camera glasses — all of it slowly repurposed into an undercover operation against loneliness.

A private investigator in Chile hires someone to work as a mole at a retirement home where a client of his suspects the caretakers of elder abuse.

metas.name: Images of the World and the Inscription of War
metas.description:
The gap between what an image records and what anyone sees in it is the whole subject. Allied reconnaissance planes photographed Auschwitz in 1944 while aiming at a factory next door; the camps sat in the archive, photographed in full and entirely unnoticed, for three decades. Farocki builds the film from that one distinction, stated in evidence.

Farocki’s intriguing and troubling film explores the processes of visual perception and how they affect our understanding of history and society. In a work reminiscent of the writings of Paul Virilio and Michel Foucault, Farocki examines a range of phenomena including aerial reconnaissance photos of the Auschwitz concentration camp.

metas.name: Five Dedicated to Ozu
metas.description:
The world is watched with the story removed. Five long static shots of the Caspian shore: waves, ducks, driftwood, a dog, the moon on water. No characters, no plot — just duration and attention, dedicated to the director who taught him both. A pure test of whether framing alone is enough.

Five sequences : 1) A piece of driftwood on the seashore, carried about by the waves 2) People walking on the seashore. The oldest ones stop by, look at the sea, then go away 3) Blurry shapes on a winter beach. A herd of dogs. A l...

metas.name: Moi, un noir
metas.description:
Colonised men narrate themselves as movie stars. Young Nigerien migrants in Abidjan play themselves but dub their own lives in the voices of Edward G. Robinson and Lemmy Caution; documentary subjects seizing control of their own image and re-authoring what it shows. Ethnography turned inside out, decades before that was a method.

A life of Nigerien immigrants in Abidjan, Ivory Coast within a week.

metas.name: The Seasons
metas.description:
An Armenian mountain year unfolds as pure rhythm. Shepherds swept downriver clutching sheep, hay sleds flying downhill, a wedding, a flock pouring over a ridge — Pelechian's "distance montage" builds meaning between shots that never touch. Thirty minutes, no dialogue, elemental.

Film-essay about shepherds living in the Armenian highlands, about the contradiction and the harmony between man and nature.

metas.name: Where Is the Friend's House?
metas.description:
A child's errand is given the scale of an epic. A boy takes the wrong notebook home from school and walks to the next village to return it before his friend is expelled; every adult is a locked door. It may be the simplest film imaginable and also the most suspenseful — proof that simplicity can hit as hard as complexity.

Eight-year-old Ahmed has mistakenly taken his friend Mohammad's notebook. He wants to return it, or else his friend will be expelled from school. The boy determinedly sets out to find Mohammad's home in the neighbouring village.

metas.name: The Quince Tree Sun
metas.description:
A painter races light he knows he'll lose. Antonio López sets up his easel before a quince tree each autumn day, marking the fruit's fall with threads and plumb lines while the radio murmurs the world; a film about trying to fix in paint a subject that changes by the hour. Process cinema at its most patient.

The artist Antonio López tries to capture the sunlight hitting his quince tree all autumn, but the struggle seems futile.

metas.name: Kuroneko
metas.description:
A ghost story is staged like Noh theatre in a bamboo grove. A mother and daughter-in-law, murdered by samurai, return as cat-spirits sworn to drink samurai blood — until one victim is their own son and husband. Mist, wire-work leaps, and vengeance colliding with the vow that powers it.

Two women are raped and killed by samurai soldiers. Soon they reappear as vengeful ghosts who seduce and brutally murder the passing samurai.

metas.name: The Naked Island
metas.description:
A family's whole existence is hauling water uphill. On a barren Seto Inland Sea island with no fresh water, parents row to the mainland and carry buckets up the slope, plant by plant, in near-total silence. Endurance, yes — but filmed as choreography, not punishment; it plays like a folk song about labour.

A family of four are the sole inhabitants of a small island where they struggle each day to irrigate their crops.

metas.name: An Actor's Revenge
metas.description:
Kabuki artifice is turned into a weapon. An onnagata — a male actor who plays women — hunts the three men who destroyed his parents, never leaving character onstage or off; Ichikawa shoots it in widescreen tableaux where the theatrical sets and the "real" streets obey the same painted logic. Maximalism with a revenge plot for a spine.

Yukinojo, a Kabuki actor, seeks revenge by destroying the three men who caused the deaths of his parents. Also involved are the daughter of one of Yukinojo's targets, two master thieves, and a swordsman who himself is out to kill ...

metas.name: Seconds
metas.description:
A man buys a new body and finds the old one included. A bored banker fakes his death, gets a younger face (Rock Hudson) and a ready-made artist's life from a courteous corporation — and discovers the self isn't a component that swaps. The most paranoid American film of its decade, and its camera tilts like the ground is unreliable.

A sinister company transforms a plain client.

metas.name: The Swimmer
metas.description:
A suburb is revealed one swimming pool at a time. Burt Lancaster, in trunks, decides to "swim home" across the county through his neighbours' pools; each stop strips another layer off the story he's telling about himself. A single afternoon, a single journey, and the life he describes turns out to be a story he has been telling himself the whole way.

A man spends a summer day swimming home via all the pools in his quiet suburban neighborhood.

metas.name: Morvern Callar
metas.description:
Grief is processed through a dead boyfriend's mixtape. A supermarket worker wakes to find he has killed himself, left her his novel's manuscript and a compilation tape; she sends the novel out under her own name and listens her way across Spain. The tape does the character work.

After her beloved boyfriend's suicide, a mourning supermarket worker and her best friend hit the road in Scotland, but find that grief is something that you can't run away from forever.

metas.name: A Tale of the Wind
metas.description:
An 89-year-old filmmaker chases the one subject that can't be framed. Ivens, making films since 1928 and asthmatic all his life, travels to China to film the wind — waiting with desert nomads, schoolchildren and a terracotta army for the invisible to move something visible. His last film; the invisible subject turns out to be weather itself.

An elderly, asthmatic filmmaker travels to China, hoping to film the wind.

metas.name: Notre musique
metas.description:
The film is arranged as Hell, Purgatory, Heaven. Hell is a montage of war footage; Purgatory is a literary conference in Sarajevo where Godard lectures on text and image while Olga, a young journalist, asks the wrong questions; Heaven is a guarded lakeside garden. The middle panel's lecture — shot and reverse-shot treated as an ethical problem — is the heart of it.

An indictment of modern times divided into three "kingdoms": "Enfer" ("Hell"), "Purgatoire" ("Purgatory") and "Paradis" ("Paradise").

metas.name: Histoire(s) du cinéma
metas.description: One man spends a decade re-editing the entire century of cinema inside his own head. Eight parts of layered clips, paintings, text and whispered commentary: film history as an apparatus that showed everything and recognised almost nothing, assembled as a kind of autobiography. A monument; take it in parts, the way it was made.

metas.name: The Adventures of Prince Achmed
metas.description:
The Arabian Nights are retold in cut-paper silhouettes, made frame by frame over three years. The oldest animated feature that survives, and it still moves like a shadow-play dream — flying horses, shape-shifting battles, a witch duel in mid-air.

A handsome prince rides a flying horse to faraway lands and embarks on magical adventures, which include befriending a witch, meeting Aladdin, battling demons and falling in love with a princess.

metas.name: Son of the White Mare
metas.description:
A Hungarian folk tale becomes a full psychedelic cosmology. A hero raised by a white mare descends to the underworld to free three princesses; every frame is saturated folk-art geometry, trees become faces, cities become breasts, colours carry the mythology. Folk-art psychedelia, in animation.

In this dreamlike Hungarian folk myth, a horse goddess gives birth to three powerful brothers who set out into the Underworld to save three princesses from three evil dragons and reclaim their ancestors' lost kingdom.

metas.name: Sita Sings the Blues
metas.description:
The Ramayana is told four ways at once: 1920s blues vocals by Annette Hanshaw, shadow-puppet narrators bickering over the plot, lush vector animation, and the director's own breakup drawn in squiggles — the same story retold through four different forms, and they don't agree.

An animated version of the epic Indian tale of Ramayana set to the 1920s jazz vocals of Annette Hanshaw.

metas.name: Night on the Galactic Railroad
metas.description:
Two cat schoolboys ride a train through the Milky Way, visiting the dead. Kenji Miyazawa's novel rendered in slow, starlit melancholy; the stops along the line are all the ways people leave. A quiet, starlit cosmology.

Two kittens go on a metaphysical journey on a magical railroad train.

metas.name: Angel's Egg
metas.description:
A girl carries an egg she will not explain, through a drowned Gothic city, followed by a man carrying a cross-shaped weapon. Almost no dialogue; rain, fossils, water tanks full of shadow fish. Oshii lost his faith and made this instead of a sermon.

A mysterious young girl wanders a desolate, otherworldly landscape, carrying a large egg.

metas.name: Belladonna of Sadness
metas.description:
A medieval witch's rise and destruction plays out in watercolours that keep dissolving. A peasant woman bargains with the Devil across still paintings that pan, bleed and occasionally erupt into full animation and psychedelic rock. Suppressed for decades, restored now — maximalism on paper.

After being raped by an evil feudal lord and subsequently getting banished from her village, a peasant girl makes a pact with the Devil to gain magical powers and take her revenge.

metas.name: Millennium Actress
metas.description:
A retired actress's memories are edited as the films she starred in. Two documentary makers interview her, and each recollection deposits them inside the scene — feudal Japan, wartime, a space launch — while her one lost love stays a frame ahead. A life story in which the biography on screen keeps being remade by the one underneath.

A TV interviewer and his cameraman meet a former actress and travel through her memories and career.

metas.name: Ghost in the Shell
metas.description:
A cyborg major hunts a hacker who may be the first digital life-form, in long rain-slick silences between the action. This is the film that made "what counts as a self when every layer is replaceable" into mainstream science fiction, and it argues by canal boat and museum tree as much as by dialogue.

A cyborg policewoman and her partner hunt a mysterious and powerful hacker called the Puppet Master.

metas.name: Ghost in the Shell 2: Innocence
metas.description:
A detective and his mostly-robotic partner investigate murdered dolls that begged to die. Dense and strange: every character quotes philosophy at each other while the camera orbits ball-jointed gynoids in a festival parade that took a year to animate. Questions about what can be seen and what can be known, embodied in dolls.

In the year 2032, Batô, a cyborg detective for the anti-terrorist unit Public Security Section 9, investigates the case of a female robot--one created solely for sexual pleasure--who slaughtered her owner.

metas.name: Mind Game
metas.description:
A failed manga artist dies, tells God off, and claws back to life at maximum velocity. The style mutates per scene — rotoscope, crayon, photo-collage — and the finale is a many-minute sprint through every life he hasn't lived yet. Pure forward motion, nothing gritty about it.

After a deadly encounter with two yakuza, a loser with a crush on his childhood girlfriend goes to heaven and back, embarking on a psychedelic self-discovery experience with her and his friends.

metas.name: Redline
metas.description:
The most dangerous race in the galaxy is drawn by hand over seven years. A pompadoured driver, a fascist robot planet, cars that deform like taffy at speed; there is no CGI sheen anywhere, just 100,000 drawings insisting that velocity is a drawing problem.

A story about the most popular racing event in the galaxy, the Redline, and the various racers who compete in it.

metas.name: Inu-Oh
metas.description:
A cursed, contorted Heian-era dancer and a blind biwa player invent rock concerts in 14th-century Kyoto. Their retellings of the Tales of the Heike make the dead visible to the crowd — and to Inu-Oh himself, whose body straightens as the buried stories get heard. Music becomes the instrument that brings the buried stories to light.

A cursed dancer and a musician stun society with electrifying concerts in this animated rock opera.

metas.name: Only Yesterday
metas.description:
A 27-year-old office worker travels with her 10-year-old self as a permanent passenger. Taeko takes a farm holiday; every adult decision gets cross-examined by the child who wanted fractions explained and a boy to glance at her. Two ages of one person, observing each other, neither in charge.

A twenty-seven-year-old office worker travels to the countryside while reminiscing about her childhood in Tokyo.

metas.name: The Boy and the Heron
metas.description:
A boy follows a grey heron into a tower where time pools and the dead curate worlds. Miyazaki's most autobiographical film is also his strangest: warplanes, pelicans, parakeets with knives, and a grand-uncle maintaining a stack of blocks that is either the universe or a career.

In the wake of his mother's death and his father's remarriage, a headstrong boy ventures into a dreamlike world shared by the living and the dead in search of his missing stepmother.

metas.name: Whisper of the Heart
metas.description:
A girl reverse-engineers a boy from the checkout cards in library books. Shizuku notices the same name borrowed every book before her, and the hunt becomes a film about deciding to make things — she writes a novel to find out if she can. A gentle film, and at its heart it's about building skill into a life.

A love story between a girl who loves reading books and a boy who has previously checked out all of the library books she chooses.

metas.name: The Red Turtle
metas.description:
A castaway's whole life unfolds on one island, without a word of dialogue. A man, a giant red turtle that keeps wrecking his rafts, and then a transformation the film simply places before you like weather. Ghibli co-produced; the water is drawn with a painter's patience.

A man is shipwrecked on a deserted island and encounters a big red turtle, which changes his life.

metas.name: The Missing Picture
metas.description:
A genocide whose footage doesn't exist is rebuilt in clay. Panh's family died under the Khmer Rouge; the propaganda reels show smiling peasants, so he carves little clay figures and dioramas to stand where the record is missing. The archive that exists, set against the reality that went unrecorded — and it is a documentary.

Rithy Panh uses clay figures, archival footage, and his narration to recreate the atrocities Cambodia's Khmer Rouge committed between 1975 and 1979.

metas.name: When the Wind Blows
metas.description:
A retired couple prepares for nuclear war with government pamphlets and total faith in procedure. Hand-drawn, gentle, funny — Jim keeps saying the authorities know best while the fallout does its work. Raymond Briggs wrote it as a cartoon; it lands like a memorial.

A naive elderly British rural couple survive the initial onslaught of a nuclear war.

metas.name: World of Tomorrow
metas.description:
A little girl is visited by her own clone from 227 years later, who explains the future in a level, broken monotone. Seventeen minutes, stick figures, and the whole apparatus of memory-copying, failed immortality and inherited feeling. Seventeen minutes long, and it earns its brevity.

A little girl is taken on a mind-bending tour of her distant future.

metas.name: Soul
metas.description:
A jazz pianist dies on the day of his break and has to argue his way out of the afterlife's intake office. The Great Before assigns personalities like case files; Joe's file keeps insisting the meaning was in the ordinary takes. Pixar's most explicit film about what a life is for, hidden inside its most musical one.

Joe is a middle-school band teacher whose life hasn't quite gone the way he expected. His true passion is jazz. But when he travels to another realm to help someone find their passion, he soon discovers what it means to have soul.

metas.name: Lily and Jim
metas.description:
A blind date is narrated by both daters at once, in split-screen stick figures, each privately misreading the other in real time. Thirteen minutes, made when he was barely out of film school, and the dual-internal-monologue structure is already fully formed.

A blind date ends in disaster.

metas.name: Billy's Balloon
metas.description:
Toddlers are attacked by their own balloons, for no reason, in a park, while the parents don't notice. Five minutes, student-film crude, and still the purest statement of a comic physics: the world is soft, round, and hostile.

A boy and his balloon.

metas.name: Rejected
metas.description:
An animator's commissioned ad cartoons are rejected one by one as they — and he — visibly fall apart. It starts with a banana announcing "my spoon is too big" and ends with the paper universe collapsing, blood pooling in the margins. Oscar-nominated, quoted for a quarter century, and it still feels unstable.

In the spring of 1999, the Family Learning Channel commissioned animator Don Hertzfeldt to produce promotional segments for their network. The cartoons were completed in five weeks. The Family Learning Channel rejected all of them upon review, and they were never aired...

metas.name: The Meaning of Life
metas.description:
All of evolution and human history unrolls as a twelve-minute time-lapse that refuses to land on us. Creatures morph across geological time, crowds become patterns, patterns become individuals again; the title is the dare, and the ending is the shrug the title earns.

A sprawling look at the evolution of humankind, over the course of a billion years.

metas.name: Everything Will Be OK
metas.description:
Bill, an ordinary man, finds his days — window light, a cough, a strange feeling in the street — start arriving out of order as an unnamed illness takes his memory apart. Sunny on the surface, and quietly frightening underneath.

A series of dark and troubling events forces Bill to reckon with the meaning of his life - or lack thereof.

metas.name: I Am So Proud of You
metas.description: Bill's family history is told as a hereditary weather system: a mother, a man split into two by a train, a cousin in a rocket, the same darkness handed down like furniture. The narration, by now pure prose, carries it all.

metas.name: Wisdom Teeth
metas.description:
A man has a wisdom tooth pulled, and his friend asks to pull the stitches. Five minutes, one dental thread, escalating commitment to a single bad idea.

Nigel does his best to help with his friend's simple request.

metas.name: World of Tomorrow Episode Two: The Burden of Other People's Thoughts
metas.description:
Little Emily travels into the mind of her older clone, where memories are stored as literal rooms other people have moved into. Instead of travelling forward, the film goes inward: identity as a house full of other people's furniture.

Emily is visited by a backup clone of herself from the even-more distant future, as they must venture into each other's psyches in order to restore the clone's deteriorating mind.

metas.name: World of Tomorrow Episode Three: The Absent Destinations of David Prime
metas.description:
A time-travelling husband, erased from his own timeline, sends instructions backward to a wife who no longer remembers him. An intricate love story conducted entirely through messages left in the wrong years.

A hidden memory sends David across the far reaches of time and space to solve a deadly mystery involving his time-traveling future selves.

metas.name: Me
metas.description:
In twenty-two nearly wordless minutes, a musical plays out about a self absorbing everything it touches. His newest: a round character rolls through a hand-drawn world converting people, places and finally the film itself into more of himself. After thirty years of drawing other people's inner lives, this is the one about the ego as a closed system — a self that only ever takes in more of itself.

A musical odyssey about generational trauma and the retreat of humanity into itself.

metas.name: Babette's Feast
metas.description:
Grace arrives here in the form of a dinner. Two austere Danish sisters who have refused every pleasure take in a refugee cook; her one act of revenge against a life of plain food is a full Parisian feast for the sect that saved her. Faith as belonging, food as love language, and an ending where nobody is punished for enjoying themselves.

During the late 19th century, a strict religious community in a Danish village takes in a French refugee from the Franco-Prussian War as a servant to the late pastor's daughters.

metas.name: The Taste of Things
metas.description:
A marriage is conducted in a kitchen over twenty years. A cook and the gourmet who employs and adores her; the film is mostly the work itself — stocks, vol-au-vent, hands passing tools without looking. Love that works, shown as competence shared. Its director works here at the opposite pole of life from the longing and heat he once filmed.

The story of Eugenie, an esteemed cook, and Dodin - the fine gourmet chef she has been working for over the last 20 years.
